title: [Wayland] Launch feedback creates two entries in the task manager when I open certain flatpaks from flathub or when I open apps via shortcuts created with kmenuedit
line: Launching an app from a custom or renamed desktop file no longer shows two Task Manager entries while it starts.
explanation: KWin announces a launch to the Task Manager under the app id of the desktop file that was launched (e.g. mykonsole), but the window that opens reports its own app id (org.kde.konsole). The Task Manager matches startups to windows by app id, so it showed the startup next to the window entry, and KWin only ended the startup when the window was mapped, a few frames after the window entry appeared. Now KWin ends the Task Manager startup as soon as the window uses the launch's activation token (sent right after its first commit), so the window entry takes its place; the cursor launch feedback still ends at map time as before.

commits.message:
xdgactivation: end the task manager startup once its token is used

When the window's app id differs from the launched desktop file, the
task manager can't match it to the startup and shows both until the
window is mapped. End that startup once the window uses its token.

BUG: 453776

media.caption: Panel frames (30 fps) while launching a MyKonsole desktop file (Exec=konsole) from KRunner: the startup entry and the Konsole window entry side by side, then an empty gap
Same launch with the fix: one entry that turns into the Konsole window entry in place
Same launch with the fix, slowed down 4x

review.text: Resetting m_activation in XdgActivationV1Integration::activateSurface() before window->readyForPainting() is a narrow timing workaround that does not properly fix Bug 453776 and degrades launch feedback semantics for all Wayland apps. It still leaves pinned launchers showing two Task Manager entries for the entire startup duration before a surface exists (a core case for kmenuedit shortcuts, Okular, and renamed Flatpaks) and does not help apps that do not send xdg_activation_v1.activate before their first buffer commit. At the same time, ending plasma_activation_feedback before the window is ready for painting prematurely cuts off Task Manager startup feedback for normal matching apps and desynchronizes it from cursor launch feedback.
changes: Do not reset m_activation in activateSurface() before window->readyForPainting(); keep plasma_activation_feedback tied to the window actually becoming ready/mapped.

Address the actual appId/desktop-file mismatch instead: resolve desktop-file aliases such as X-KDE-AliasFor and X-Flatpak-RenamedFrom in KWin/KIO/libtaskmanager (as in kwin!3386), and ensure kmenuedit shortcuts preserve or set StartupWMClass/X-KDE-AliasFor (or match via Exec in libtaskmanager) so both pinned and unpinned launches match their startup task.
